newsitem.title: UK: BSkyB down as report raises digital TV fears.
newsitem.headline: BSkyB down as report raises digital TV fears.

text.p: Shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc fell in early trade on Wednesday after a press report said the company would be excluded from a consortium bidding for a UK digital television license.
The stock was down 23p or four percent at 543-1/2 by 0707 GMT in volume of 164,800 shares.

The Financial Times said the Independent Television Commission, the UK broadcasting watchdog, was to tell BSkyB to drop its equity stake in the British Digital group, because it risked concentrating too much power in the TV sector.
The group also includes Carlton Communications Plc and Granada Group Plc.
The report provided a second setback for BSkyB shares, the day after its highly-rated chief executive Sam Chisolm announced that he would step down at the end of the year on medical grounds.
The FT's influential Lex column said Chisolm would be a "hard act to follow" and that there was "substantial scope for disappointment" in the stock, which was trading on an above-average rating.
No-one at BSkyB was immediately available for comment.
